We have seen the three vows taken by Swami Ramanujar at the mortal remains of Aalavandaar at Sri Rangam. After returning to Kanchipuram, Swami Ramanujar got married to a woman named Rakshambal. At the age of 28, Swami Ramanujar's mother attained Paramapadam. After his mother attained Paramapadam, Swami Ramanujar continued his education under the disciples of Aalavandaar and continued performing kainkaryam to Sri Varadaraja Perumal at Kanchipuram. 


At Kanchipuram, Swami Ramanujar first met Tirukacchi Nambigal, who was another disciple of Aalavandaar. Although Tirukacchi Nambigal was not a brahmin, he was treated with immense respect because of his simple-minded and broad-minded approach. Tirukacchi Nambigal was allowed to perform chamara seva to Sri Varadaraja Perumal. It is said that Varadaraja Perumal used to converse with Tirukacchi Nambigal during the time in which he used to perform chamara seva. Swami Ramanujar was anxious to meet Tirukacchi Nambigal.



When Swami Ramanujar first met Tirukacchi Nambi, he invited Tirukacchi Nambigal to come over to his house for a meal. Swami Ramanujar's house was situated in the periphery of the Varadaraja Perumal Temple, which is humongous. Tirukacchi Nambigal accepted the invite and told Swami Ramanujar that he would love to come to his place for a meal. He said he would enter the following day for lunch. The next day, near lunchtime, Swami Ramanujar was anxiously awaiting the arrival of Tirukacchi Nambigal. As he was very anxious, he told his wife Rakshambal that he would go and check on where their guest was situated and left the house. Soon Tirukacchi Nambigal arrived at Swami Ramanujar's house. Rakashambal was a very narrow-minded woman. She knew that Tirukacchi Nambigal was not a brahmin. Hence, she asked him to sit outside the house's central courtyard. She then asked him if he had anything to eat. He replied that he had come to their home as Swami Ramanujar had invited him for lunch. She then spread out a banana leaf in the outer courtyard and served his meal very scantily. 


Tirukacchi Nambigal thanked her for the meal and left. As soon as Tirukacchi Nambigal had left the house, Rakshambal pushed the banana leaf with a stick, cleaned the area with cow dung, broke the earthen vessels in which she had prepared meals for Tirukacchi Nambigal, and took a bath to cleanse herself. When Swami Ramanujar returned, he noticed that Rakshambal's hair was untied and was wet. He asked if Tirukacchi Nambigal had come to the house. Rakshambal, with a disgusted face, tells Swami Ramanujar that the vaishya had come and she had served him food. She was disgusted by the fact that her husband wanted to engage himself with the likes of a lower caste man.


Swami Ramanujar felt insulted by her behavior but did not speak up as he did not wish to incite violence inside the household. A few days passed by, and Swami Ramanujar ran into Tirukacchi Nambigal inside the temple, and with folded hands, he pleaded for forgiveness for his wife's actions. He told Tirukacchi Nambigal that he had some questions about his dharmam that he would like to talk about with him. Tirukacchi Nambigal said he was on his way to perform chamara seva to Varadaraja Perumal and told Swami Ramanujar he would ask the Lord, as He is all-knowing. 


As Tiukacchi Nambigal waved the chamaram to the Lord, the Lord sensed a longing emanating from Tirukacchi Nambigal and asked him if he had any questions to ask Him. Tirukacchi Nambigal told the Lord that the questions were not his but those of Swami Ramanujar. Varadaraja Perumal is then supposed to have said Tirukacchi Nambigal's six statements as follows:
Ahameva Paramtatvam
Darshanam bedameva cha
Upayeshu Prapatti syaath
Anthima Smrithi Varjanam
Dehaa Vasaane Mukti Syaath
Purnacharya Samashrayaha
These six statements can be interpreted in the following way:

Ahameva Paratatvam: The Lord is the ultimate truth, and He is all-knowing.
Darshanam Bedameva cha: This statement is interpreted by the statement of " Tat Tvam Asi. " The jeevaathma is always independent of the Paramaathma but longs to reach the Paramaathma.

Upayeshu Prapatti Syaath: To be truly free from the cycle of life and death, one must perform Prapatti to the Lord at the hands of an Acharya.

Anthima Smrithi Varjanam: According to shastras, one will genuinely attain moksham when they remember the Lord at the time before the jeevaathma leaves the mortal body. As it is difficult for everyone to remember the Lord during Kaliyugam, the Lord tells Tirukacchi Nambi that He would remember those on their deathbed if they had performed Prapatti during their lifetime.

Dehaa Vasaane Mukthi Syaath: After death, the soul is weighed to see if it is fit to attain moksham. If the jeevaathma in its lifetime had performed Prapatti, it would gain direct access into Vaikuntham to thrive in the presence of the Lord eternally.

Purnacharya Samashrayaha: Taking refuge at the feet of an Acharya and getting panchasamskaaram done by his hands is the means to Prapatti.


After his conversation with Varadaraja Perumal, Tirukacchi Nambigal informs Swami Ramanujar about his conversation with the Lord, sharing the six statements the Lord made. Swami Ramanujar immediately rushes to meet Periya Nambi at  Sri Rangam. At the same time, Ranganatha Perumal instructs Periya Nambi to perform panchasamskaaram to Swami Ramanujar. The two meet at Maduranthankam's Yeri Kaatha Raamar Perumal temple, where Periya Nambi performed panchasamskaaram to Swami Ramanujar and initiated him into Sri Vaishnava Parampara.
